messages:
maya (Support): FYI customer reported indexing failures across multiple jobs since ~02:00 UTC. Error shows: \"vector dim 1024 != expected 1536\". They say this started right after yesterday's embeddings model canary. Need triage.

sam (Eng Oncall): Copy of the error payload? sample request/response? Which pipeline job id? severity?

maya (Support): Paste from logs: 
```
IndexerJob[job=ingest-789] ERROR: failed to write batch 12/256: validation_error: incompatible_vector: expected_dim=1536 got_dim=1024
stack: IndexWriter::validate_vector_size at writer.rs:421
```
Customer job id: ingress-20260314-42, they attached a sample record. They call our embeddings endpoint with model param `embed-ada-1536` (old) but our canary changed default to `embed-large-v2` which returns 1024.

leo (Indexer): That mismatch screams model-version drift. Two likely paths: 1) client libraries got mixed defaults during rolling deploy so some workers call the new model, others use old — then batching merges vectors. 2) Our schema migration for the vector DB (applied 01:45 UTC) now enforces strict dims. db-bot should have flagged the migration window.

db-bot: Alert: schema-migration-vecdb applied to cluster vec-prod-3 at 01:47:12 UTC. Validation mode=STRICT, expected_vector_dim=1536. No rollback executed.

sam (Eng Oncall): Can we reproduce quickly? Maya, can you run a single doc through the exact pipeline with the canary model config? Provide curl we can run.

maya (Support): Here's the curl the ingest service uses (simplified):
```
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"embed-large-v2","input":"hello world"}'
```
Response for canary host: `{\"data\":[{\"embedding\":[...1024 floats...] }] }`
Response for old host (pinned): `{\"data\":[{\"embedding\":[...1536 floats...] }] }`

leo (Indexer): Repro steps look solid. Hypothesis: indexer pool has long-lived connections to the embeddings backend; during the canary a subset of requests were routed to new model variant. Batching logic concatenates embeddings per-request but then tries to write batch into vecdb assuming uniform dim. So mixed dims show up when a batch contains both model outputs.

sam (Eng Oncall): Short-term mitigation (<=1 hour): 1) Route indexing pipeline traffic to pinned model `embed-legacy-1536` via routing policy. 2) Enable pre-write validation to drop mixed-dim batches and route to dead-letter queue (DLQ) so we don't fail entire batch. 3) Temporarily set vecdb to accept either by switching validation to PERMISSIVE (requires DBA change). Which is fastest?

leo (Indexer): Routing + DLQ is safest. DB PERMISSIVE needs ops approval and snapshot first. I can flip routing rule in ~10m if eng approves. Sam, can you update the routing policy?

sam (Eng Oncall): On it. Pinned rule created: `route: indexers -> embed-legacy-1536` (applied to service `indexer-v2`) 
Action log: `routing-change-1781023600`

maya (Support): Customer confirmed reduced failures after routing change, but backlog of ~800k records failed earlier and require backfill. They want ETA and risk.

leo (Indexer): Backfill plan (proposal):
- snapshot vecdb collection `kb_docs_v1` -> snapshot_id `snap-1781023700`
- create backfill workers on Dedicated nodes (no shared hosts) with controlled concurrency: concurrency=8, batch_size=32, pause_on_rate=200ms
- re-embed documents using pinned model `embed-legacy-1536` to match existing vectors OR choose to re-embed entire collection to new 1024-dim model and migrate to a new collection.
- prefer re-embedding to legacy for minimal client changes. Steps:
  1) spin up `indexer-backfill-1536` job referencing snapshot and pinned model
  2) run small pilot on shard 0 (5k docs), verify vector write and nearest-neighbor sanity checks
  3) full run with monitoring and throttling, estimate time ~18-24 hours at concurrency above.

sam (Eng Oncall): Ops checklist: ensure quota for embeddings for backfill (estimated 800k * 1536 tokens ~= cost estimate), request Dedicated pool for backfill to avoid noisy-neighbor throttles. Also add a guard to fail gracefully if we spot a different dim at write time.

maya (Support): Customer asked about data safety: will we lose vectors? They saw some partial writes.

leo (Indexer): Partial writes only happened when batches were rejected; no in-place overwrites. Snapshot + backfill will restore full coverage. We'll add post-backfill validation to check counts and sample similarity metrics.

sam (Eng Oncall): Owners & timeline:
- Routing & short-term DLQ fix: sam (done)
- Backfill job + pilot: leo (owner) — pilot in 2 hours, full run after pilot signoff
- Ops snapshot & permissive test: infra oncall (TBD)
- Support comms / billing questions: maya
Ticket created: PROJ-3459 (priority P1 -> customer SLA impacted).

leo (Indexer): Backfill pilot command (internal):
```
python tools/backfill_run.py \
  --snapshot snap-1781023700 \
  --collection kb_docs_v1 \
  --model embed-legacy-1536 \
  --concurrency 8 \
  --batch-size 32 \
  --dry-run false
```
I'll post results from pilot shard in this thread.

db-bot: Note: schedule maintenance window if switching vecdb validation to PERMISSIVE. Ops approval required.

sam (Eng Oncall): Also followup: add a CI check to client libs so default model isn't changed implicitly by deploys (test that embedding dim remains stable for pinned names). Filing infra ticket.

maya (Support): Customer updated: appreciates the routing change, asked for an ETA for backfill + rough cost estimate. I'll feed them the plan and owners.

leo (Indexer): Pilot started -> will report in ~30m. If pilot passes, full backfill run scheduled overnight with dedicated pool.

sam (Eng Oncall): Thanks team. Postmortem action items: better deploy rollback if model dim changes, add early-detection telemetry for mixed-dim batches, and make batch writes tolerant (DLQ) by default.

maya (Support): Closing loop with customer now. Will update ticket PROJ-3459 with the backfill plan and owners.

leo (Indexer): Pilot results: pilot 5k docs -> success, 0 write errors after routing fix, mean ingest latency 18ms/doc. Scheduling full backfill 03:00 UTC.

maya (Support): Customer acked schedule. Marking as monitored until backfill completes.

sam (Eng Oncall): Leaving notes: root cause = model canary changed default without pinning, causing mixed-dim outputs in pooled batching. Remediations in place. Follow-ups tracked in PROJ-3459.
